explanation: Use the sorted characters of a word as its grouping key. Return every group, including singleton groups, as required by this Blind75 contract.
timeComplexity: O(N + S log(L+1) + N L log(N+1)) upper bound for N words, S total characters, and maximum length L. Keys are sorted, then inserted into std::map: each ordered-map lookup makes O(log(N+1)) string comparisons of up to L characters.
spaceComplexity: O(N+S) storage for sorted keys and grouped string copies; the returned groups also copy the original strings. Iterating the map by value can temporarily copy one group, still within this bound.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 C++ algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: A sorted-character key is equal exactly for words with the same character multiset. Appending each original word to its key’s bucket therefore creates all anagram classes, with every input occurrence present once. Returning all buckets retains singleton classes as this contract requires.
walkthrough: For ["arc","rat","car","tar","owl"], keys acr,art,acr,art,low create groups ["arc","car"],["rat","tar"],["owl"]. Return all three groups, including the singleton owl.
edgeCases: Singleton groups are included, unlike the EPI variant.
Repeated identical words remain repeated entries.
Group order and word order within a group are unrestricted.
